facts.statement: Yunganglong is an extinct basal hadrosauroid dinosaur found in the early Late Cretaceous lower Zhumapu Formation of Zuoyun County, Shanxi Province, northeastern China.
facts.quote: Yunganglong is an extinct genus of basal hadrosauroid dinosaur known from the early Late Cretaceous lower Zhumapu Formation of Zuoyun County, Shanxi Province of northeastern China.

facts.statement: Yunganglong was first described and named by a team of eight researchers led by Run-Fu Wang in 2013.
facts.quote: Yunganglong was first described and named by Run-Fu Wang, Hai-Lu You, Shi-Chao Xu, Suo-Zhu Wang, Jian Yi, Li-Juan Xie, Lei Jia and Ya-Xian Li in 2013

facts.statement: The genus name honors the Yungang Grottoes, a UNESCO World Heritage site located about 50 km from the fossil discovery site, and includes the Chinese word for 'dragon'.
facts.quote: The generic name honors Yungang Grottoes, a UNESCO World Heritage site built in the 5th and 6th centuries about 50 km east of the fossil locality, and derived from long meaning "dragon" in Chinese.

facts.statement: The species name refers to the city of Datong in northern Shanxi Province, where the holotype specimen was discovered.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to the city of Datong, located in northern Shanxi province, where the holotype was found.

facts.statement: The dinosaur is known only from a single disarticulated partial skeleton, holotype SXMG V 00001, which is housed at the Shanxi Museum of Geology.
facts.quote: Yunganglong is known solely from the holotype SXMG V 00001, field number ZY007, an associated but disarticulated partial skeleton housed at the Shanxi Museum of Geology.

facts.statement: The fossils were collected in 2011 as part of a project initiated by the Department of Land and Resources of Shanxi Province to supply the Shanxi Museum of Geology.
facts.quote: The remains were collected in 2011 from Locality 7 of the Zhumapu Formation, as a part of a project to find dinosaurs for the Shanxi Museum of Geology, initiated by the Department of Land and Resources of Shanxi Province.

facts.statement: In addition to the Yunganglong holotype, ankylosaur and ceratopsian fossils were found at the same localities.
facts.quote: Other than SXMG V 00001, ankylosaur and ceratopsian remains were found from the newly discovered localities.

facts.statement: The genus Yunganglong contains only one known species, Yunganglong datongensis.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Yunganglong datongensis.

facts.statement: Yunganglong is classified within the superfamily Hadrosauroidea.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Hadrosauroidea

facts.statement: Yunganglong belongs to the infraorder Iguanodontia.
facts.quote: infraordo: Iguanodontia

facts.statement: Yunganglong possessed a skull that was relatively wide and low.
facts.quote: The skull of Yunganglong is relatively wide and low.

facts.statement: The caudal surface of the supraoccipital bone in Yunganglong is inclined steeply forward at approximately 45 degrees, distinguishing it from more primitive relatives where it is nearly vertical.
facts.quote: The caudal surface of the supraoccipital in Yunganglong and more advanced hadrosauroids is inclined steeply forward at approximately 45°, while nearly vertical in Jintasaurus and less derived Hadrosauriformes.

facts.statement: Yunganglong was a ground-dwelling herbivore capable of both bipedal and quadrupedal locomotion.
facts.quote: Like other hadrosauroids, Yunganglong was a ground-dwelling herbivore that could walk bipedally, and could stand on all four legs.

facts.statement: Fossils of Yunganglong were found in the lower Zhumapu Formation in Zuoyun County, Shanxi Province, in northeastern China.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en la zona inferior de la Formación Zhumapu en el condado de Zuoyun, provincia de Shanxi en el noreste de China.

facts.statement: Yunganglong lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, approximately 100 to 95 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage.
facts.quote: vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 100 y 95 millones de años durante el Cenomaniense

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Yunganglog as more advanced than Probactrosaurus, within an unresolved group with other early hadrosauroids like Jintasaurus and Protohadros.
facts.quote: In the strict consensus tree, Yunganglong was recovered as more advanced than Probactrosaurus, in an unresolved polytomy with Jintasaurus, Protohadros, Nanyangosaurus, Shuangmiaosaurus, Levnesovia, Bactrosaurus, Tanius, Telmatosaurus and the clade formed by Aralosaurus and Hadrosauridae.

facts.statement: The genus Yunganglong was described and named by a team of eight researchers in 2013.
facts.quote: Yunganglong fue descrito y nombrado originalmente por Run-Fu Wang, Hai-Lu You, Shi-Chao Xu, Suo-Zhu Wang, Jian Yi, Li-Juan Xie, Lei Jia y Ya-Xian Li en 2013

facts.statement: The genus name honors the Yungang Grottoes, a UNESCO World Heritage site located about 50 kilometers east of the fossil site, combined with the Chinese word for 'dragon'.
facts.quote: El nombre del género honra a las Grutas de Yungang, un Patrimonio de la Humanidad construido en los siglos y cerca de 50 kilómetros al este de la localidad fósil, añadido a la palabra long que significa "dragón" en chino

facts.statement: The species name refers to the city of Datong in northern Shanxi province, where the holotype was discovered.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie se refiere a la ciudad de Datong, localizada en el norte de la provincia de Shanxi, en donde el holotipo fue hallado

facts.statement: The animal is known only from the holotype specimen SXMG V 00001, a disarticulated partial skeleton housed at the Shanxi Geological Museum.
facts.quote: Yunganglong solo es conocido a partir del espécimen holotipo SXMG V 00001, número de campo ZY007, un esqueleto parcial desarticulado hallado en asociación alojado en el Museo de Geología de Shanxi

facts.statement: Fossil remains were collected in 2011 from locality 7 of the Zhumapu Formation.
facts.quote: Los restos fueron recolectados en 2011 en la localidad 7 de la Formación Zhumapu

facts.statement: The holotype was found near Zuoyun County in the lower part of the Zhumapu Formation, which dates to the early Late Cretaceous based on biostratigraphic correlations.
facts.quote: SXMG V 00001 fue hallado en la vecindad del condado de Zuoyun, en la parte inferior de la Formación Zhumapu, que data de inicios del Cretácico Superior basándose en correlaciones bioestratigráficas

facts.statement: Remains of ankylosaurs and ceratopsians were also found at the newly discovered localities alongside the holotype.
facts.quote: Aparte de SXMG V 00001, se encontraron restos de anquilosaurios y ceratopsios en las localidades recién descubiertas

facts.statement: Strict consensus analysis places Yunganglong as more derived than Probactrosaurus, within an unresolved polytomy with several other basal hadrosauriforms and the Aralosaurus-Hadrosauridae clade.
facts.quote: En el árbol de consenso estricto, se encontró que Yunganglong es más avanzado que Probactrosaurus, en una politomía sin resolver con Jintasaurus, Protohadros, Nanyangosaurus, Shuangmiaosaurus, Levnesovia, Bactrosaurus, Tanius, Telmatosaurus y el clado formado por Aralosaurus y Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Yunganglong belongs to the parent group Hadrosauroidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Hadrosauroidea

facts.statement: The animal is classified within the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Yunganglong lived between the Cenomanian and Santonian stages, approximately 100.5 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Santonian (100.5 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: The first dinosaur record for Shanxi province was reported by Young in 1958 from two localities in Zuoyun County.
facts.quote: El primer registro de dinosaurios en la provincia de Shanxi fue reportado por Young (1958), de dos localidades en el condado de Zuoyun
